text:
maria: morning — not sure if this is related to the batching rollout but I'm seeing a spike of 502/504s and higher latency on /v1/embeddings in us-west-2. customers reporting timeouts and one support ticket shows a 'dimension mismatch' error string. fingered the embeddings route. anyone oncall?

deploy-bot: [ALERT] 1865007700 embeddings-service: 5xx-rate 14% (1m) — increased from baseline 0.5% :rotating_light:

maria: attaching a customer repro they pasted in support ticket (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \-H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' \-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \-d '{"model":"rwd-embed-2","input":["hello world"],"metadata":{"client_dim":1024}}'
```
Response: `400 Bad Request` with body: `{\"error\":\"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024\"}`

aaron_oncall: I'm taking this. timeline? Maria, did we recently change any batching / quantization config for rwd-embed-2?

maria: yes — @jess_platform rolled out `optimize-emb-batching=true` at 06:50 to reduce tokens/second cost for small requests. It tweaks `max_batch_size` and enables dynamic padding. I think it was a config flag in the runtime, non-disruptive but it touched the batching aggregator.

jen_infra: flight data from metrics-bot:
```
- embeddings-p95 latency (us-west-2): 1.2s -> 3.8s
- worker_queue_depth: 12 -> 240
- cpu-util (runner pods): 65% -> 98%
- gpu-util: 42% -> 95% on shard-3
- 5xx spike aligns with queue depth increase at 06:52
```
Queue backlog suggests batching increase created longer head-of-line blocking. Also seeing more fallback to quantized model variant shard when warm-up failed.

metrics-bot: trace id 0a1b2c: first 5xx at 06:53:12 -> increased every 30s. error message corpus includes `dimension mismatch` (~7 occurrences in last 15m) and `kv-cache keysize` (~12).

olivia_support: I pushed one of the affected customer payloads to a staging endpoint. They get the same `dimension mismatch` error consistently. Customer insists they didn't change client code — they send embedding vectors alongside request (legacy client) which used 1024 dims. Our model expects 1536. This looks like a client-side mismatch but why did it surface now? It used to succeed last week for them.

aaron_oncall: good catch. Two hypotheses: 1) batching/packing change now attempts to route mixed-dim requests to the same worker and our worker used to silently accept shorter vectors with padding, but new quantized shard rejects them; or 2) model variant routing changed and some requests are hitting a newer model (rwd-embed-2 v2) with 1536 dim while customer still sending 1024.

aaron_oncall: can we get recent rollout history? `kubectl get deploy embeddings-router -o yaml` and `kubectl rollout history`?

deploy-bot: rollout: embeddings-router @ 06:50 set flag `optimize-emb-batching=true`. Next deployment: none.

jen_infra: logs from router at 06:51 show this pattern:
```
[06:51:02] router: pack_batch: selected_batch_size=32, dynamic_pad=true
[06:51:02] router: assigned shard=quant-shard-3 for model=rwd-embed-2
[06:51:02] worker-23: rejected request id=abcd1234 error=embedding_dim_mismatch expected=1536 got=1024
```
So router is sending mixed-dim requests to quant-shard-3. Before the flag it did stricter binning by dim. The optimize flag apparently relaxed binning to increase packing efficiency but inadvertently merged different-dim jobs.

aaron_oncall: okay actionable: roll back `optimize-emb-batching` immediately, revert to strict dim binning, and scale up the worker pool while we triage. I'll roll back the flag then restart router pods.

aaron_oncall: executing rollback now:
```bash
# rollback flag in configmap
kubectl set env deployment/embeddings-router OPTIMIZE_EMB_BATCHING=false -n prod
kubectl rollout restart deployment/embeddings-router -n prod
# scale workers temporarily
kubectl scale deployment/embeddings-worker --replicas=12 -n prod
```

deploy-bot: acknowledged. starting restart.

maria: notifying support and affected customers that we're investigating and may do a brief restart.

(1m later)

metrics-bot: post-rollback snapshot (06:58): p95 latency down to 1.0s, queue_depth -> 8, 5xx rate -> 0.9%

aaron_oncall: confirmed error counts dropping. running a few customer repros — staging returns OK now for the previously failing payloads.

olivia_support: customer confirmed success on a test request; they will re-run full batch.

jen_infra: still seeing a handful of `kv-cache keysize` warnings, likely from a small percentage of in-flight requests during the restart. We'll keep an eye.

billing-bot: FYI — we briefly autoscaled workers; estimated incremental cost impact ~+$120 for the hour.

aaron_oncall: immediate mitigation complete. root cause: the `optimize-emb-batching` flag relaxed dim-based binning/segregation causing mixed-dim packing and routing to quantized shards that strictly enforce embedding size -> resulting in dimension mismatch 400s and increased retries leading to queue-backpressure and higher latency.

next steps / actions assigned:
- patrick_ml: (action) update the batching algorithm to never merge different embedding dims into the same pack and add unit tests — due EOD tomorrow.
- jess_platform: (action) add a canary gate for `optimize-emb-batching` to limit to <1% traffic and validate dim-binning before wider rollout. Also add a metric for "dim-mix rate" — due next week.
- jen_infra: (action) add alert on queue_depth > 50 and 5xx-rate > 3% for embeddings route to pager — doing this ASAP.
- olivia_support: (action) follow up with affected customers and confirm their SDK behavior; advise clients to drop explicit embedding vectors or migrate to new client that aligns dims — ongoing.

aaron_oncall: I'll put together a short postmortem draft and tag the above owners. Closing the incident once customers confirm prolonged stability (monitoring window 60m).

maria: thanks everyone :heart: Good catch.

(Closing note at 07:40)

aaron_oncall: closing incident — p95 latency and 5xx steady at baseline for 60m. Postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/EMB-incident-1865007777 (will fill details).
